title: Mobile: clearcoat reflects the sky at half brightness outside ReflectionProbes
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]
- v4.6.2.stable.official [71f334935]: not comparable. This test reads 0.0000 on Mobile there (Forward+ not tested on 4.6.2); the clearcoat code was reworked in 4.7 by #111464.
- Not tested on `master`. The line involved is unchanged as of 12c17c187 ([scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1694](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/12c17c187e88efa23e6bbd6689630e256eca6523/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1694)).

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.6.2) - Metal 4.0 (Mobile) - integrated Apple M5 Max (Apple9) - Apple M5 Max (18 threads) - 128.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

On the Mobile renderer, the clearcoat lobe reflects the sky (radiance map) at half the brightness it has in Forward+, when the object is outside every ReflectionProbe.

Test: a sphere with black albedo, specular 0, roughness 1, clearcoat 1 and clearcoat roughness 0, so that only the clearcoat reflects, sits under a uniform sky of radiance 0.6. At the centre of the sphere, the expected value is F0 × L = 0.04 × 0.6 = 0.024. The value is read at the centre and divided by the tonemap exposure (linear tonemapper):

| | Forward+ | Mobile |
|---|---|---|
| HDR 2D off | 0.0238 | 0.0117 |
| HDR 2D on | 0.0240 | 0.0120 |

In the same scene, a metallic mirror sphere outside the probes reflects the sky correctly on Mobile (0.588 for 0.600), so the radiance map itself is fine.

**Source (4.7.2-stable):** on Mobile, the sky radiance map is stored at 0.5× ([render_forward_mobile.cpp#L1063](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/render_forward_mobile.cpp#L1063), used at [L1136](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/forward_mobile/render_forward_mobile.cpp#L1136)). The specular and ambient lookups into it multiply by `REFLECTION_MULTIPLIER` (2.0) ([scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1618](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1618), [#L1644](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1644)), but the clearcoat lookup into the same texture does not ([#L1679](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1679)). Forward+ has the same line ([scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L1790](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L1790)), but its `REFLECTION_MULTIPLIER` is 1.0 ([scene_forward_clustered_inc.glsl#L168](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered_inc.glsl#L168)). Inside a probe, Mobile's clearcoat read does apply `REFLECTION_MULTIPLIER` ([scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl#L1391](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl#L1391)).

This is not the single-scattering difference from #117833. The clearcoat uses the Fresnel term directly, with no environment BRDF approximation ([scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1906-L1913](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_mobile/scene_forward_mobile.glsl#L1906-L1913)).

The script also measures ReflectionProbe brightness (the `probe, ...` lines), which is a separate issue and can be ignored here.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project and a scene with a `Node3D` root. Attach the script below and set the scene as the main scene.
2. Run with `--rendering-method mobile`, then with `--rendering-method forward_plus`.
3. Compare the `no probe, clearcoat sphere centre` lines (one per HDR 2D setting). Mobile prints 0.0117 and 0.0120, Forward+ prints 0.0238 and 0.0240, and the expected value is 0.0240.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

No other files are needed besides the script (no imported assets):

```gdscript
extends Node3D
# Attach to the root Node3D of an empty scene and run it, once with the Mobile renderer and
# once with Forward+ (e.g. --rendering-method mobile / forward_plus). Prints measured radiance.

const SKY := 0.6  # radiance of a uniform sky
const PANELS := {  # unshaded panels 9 m from the probe centre: direction -> radiance
	Vector3(0, 0, -1): 0.25,
	Vector3(0, 0, 1): 0.5,
	Vector3(-1, 0, 0): 0.9,
	Vector3(1, 0, 0): 1.6,
	Vector3(0, -1, 0): 1.9,
}

var env := Environment.new()
var hdr_2d := false


func _ready() -> void:
	var sky_material := ShaderMaterial.new()
	sky_material.shader = Shader.new()
	sky_material.shader.code = "shader_type sky; void sky() { COLOR = vec3(%f); }" % SKY
	env.background_mode = Environment.BG_SKY
	env.sky = Sky.new()
	env.sky.sky_material = sky_material
	env.tonemap_mode = Environment.TONE_MAPPER_LINEAR
	var world_env := WorldEnvironment.new()
	world_env.environment = env
	add_child(world_env)

	var probe := ReflectionProbe.new()  # update mode Once, box projection off
	probe.size = Vector3(20, 20, 20)
	probe.cull_mask = 1  # captures the panels and the sky, not the spheres (layer 2)
	add_child(probe)

	var panel_shader := Shader.new()
	panel_shader.code = "shader_type spatial; render_mode unshaded, cull_disabled; uniform vec3 radiance; void fragment() { ALBEDO = radiance; }"
	for dir: Vector3 in PANELS:
		var quad := QuadMesh.new()
		quad.size = Vector2(8, 8)
		quad.material = ShaderMaterial.new()
		quad.material.shader = panel_shader
		quad.material.set_shader_parameter("radiance", Vector3.ONE * PANELS[dir])
		var panel := MeshInstance3D.new()
		panel.mesh = quad
		add_child(panel)
		panel.look_at_from_position(dir * 9.0, Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.FORWARD if absf(dir.y) > 0.9 else Vector3.UP)

	var mirror := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	mirror.metallic = 1.0
	mirror.roughness = 0.0
	_sphere(mirror, Vector3.ZERO)  # inside the probe
	_sphere(mirror, Vector3(200, 0, 0))  # outside any probe: reflects the sky radiance map
	var coat := StandardMaterial3D.new()  # only the clearcoat lobe reflects anything
	coat.albedo_color = Color.BLACK
	coat.metallic_specular = 0.0
	coat.roughness = 1.0
	coat.clearcoat_enabled = true
	coat.clearcoat = 1.0
	coat.clearcoat_roughness = 0.0
	_sphere(coat, Vector3(-200, 0, 0))  # outside any probe

	var cam := Camera3D.new()  # keeps the scenario (and the probe) rendering during warm-up
	add_child(cam)
	cam.look_at_from_position(Vector3(0, 4, -16), Vector3.ZERO)

	print("%s, %s, %s" % [Engine.get_version_info().string, RenderingServer.get_current_rendering_method(), RenderingServer.get_video_adapter_name()])
	for i in 30:  # let the probe and the sky radiance map finish updating
		await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	for hdr in [false, true]:
		hdr_2d = hdr
		await _measure()
	get_tree().quit()


func _measure() -> void:
	print("-- SubViewport.use_hdr_2d = %s" % hdr_2d)
	env.tonemap_exposure = 0.25  # keeps radiance up to 4.0 below 1.0 in the capture
	var targets := PANELS.duplicate()
	targets[Vector3.UP] = SKY
	for dir: Vector3 in targets:
		# Looking out along `dir` sees the panel (or sky) directly; looking back at the mirror sphere,
		# its centre pixel reflects that same panel through the probe.
		var direct := await _radiance(dir * 5.0, dir * 6.0)
		var mirrored := await _radiance(dir * 5.0, Vector3.ZERO)
		print("probe, %-5s radiance %.2f: direct %.3f, mirror in probe %.3f, ratio %.2f" % [
				"sky" if dir == Vector3.UP else "panel", targets[dir], direct, mirrored, mirrored / direct])
	var o := Vector3(200, 0, 0)
	var sky_direct := await _radiance(o + Vector3(0, 0, -5), o + Vector3(0, 0, -10))
	var sky_mirrored := await _radiance(o + Vector3(0, 0, -5), o)
	print("no probe, sky radiance %.2f: direct %.3f, mirror %.3f, ratio %.2f" % [SKY, sky_direct, sky_mirrored, sky_mirrored / sky_direct])
	env.tonemap_exposure = 16.0
	var c := Vector3(-200, 0, 0)
	var coat := await _radiance(c + Vector3(0, 0, -5), c)
	print("no probe, clearcoat sphere centre: %.4f (expected 0.04 * %.2f = %.4f)" % [coat, SKY, 0.04 * SKY])


## Renders the view from `from` to `at` and returns the linear radiance at the centre (5x5 mean / exposure).
func _radiance(from: Vector3, at: Vector3) -> float:
	var vp := SubViewport.new()
	vp.size = Vector2i(256, 256)
	vp.use_hdr_2d = hdr_2d
	vp.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS
	add_child(vp)
	var cam := Camera3D.new()
	cam.fov = 30.0
	vp.add_child(cam)
	cam.look_at_from_position(from, at, Vector3.FORWARD if absf((at - from).normalized().y) > 0.9 else Vector3.UP)
	for i in 6:
		await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
	var img := vp.get_texture().get_image()
	vp.queue_free()
	var sum := 0.0
	for y in range(126, 131):
		for x in range(126, 131):
			var px := img.get_pixel(x, y)
			sum += px.g if hdr_2d else px.srgb_to_linear().g  # 8-bit captures are sRGB-encoded
	return sum / 25.0 / env.tonemap_exposure


func _sphere(material: Material, pos: Vector3) -> void:
	var mesh := SphereMesh.new()
	mesh.material = material
	var sphere := MeshInstance3D.new()
	sphere.mesh = mesh
	sphere.layers = 2
	sphere.position = pos
	add_child(sphere)
```

With HDR 2D off, Mobile prints `no probe, clearcoat sphere centre: 0.0117 (expected 0.04 * 0.60 = 0.0240)`, and Forward+ prints `0.0238` on the same line.

Related: #124069 (ReflectionProbe brightness on Mobile, a separate cause).
